analysis.title: GS - Lee - Macro cuRated - 23 Oct 2026
key_insights: Treasuries traded two-way on equity/AI swings and Middle East oil headlines. On Monday 2s closed +2.3bp, 5s +3.2bp, 10s +3.8bp and 30s +3.4bp (2s10s +1.5bp steeper). Oil rose with no clear headline and little Real Money or CTA buying absorbed the futures selling.

Tuesday the curve twist-flattened, led by the long bond, after a strong JGB 20y auction. Brent pushed above $110/bbl overnight before coming off its highs. With the FOMC in blackout, policy pricing barely moved: 4.25bp of hikes priced for October and 25bp by year-end.

Wednesday rates sold off in a bear-flattening move. French 10y yields topped 5% for the first time since 2002. 2s traded an 8bp range on Gulf embassy departure headlines, later clarified to apply only to some personnel in Saudi Arabia. The $13bn 20y auction had a 0.9bp tail.

Thursday saw an aggressive rally as the NDX fell roughly 3% on AI weakness (GS AI basket -23% since June) and the 10y OAT-Bund spread widened ~15bp. US 10y yields went back below 5%. 2s rallied -19bp, 5s -20.7bp, 10s -19.3bp and 30s -15.2bp. 1y1y fell ~24bp to ~4.60% and Dec FOMC traded as low as 18bp of cumulative hikes before settling near 22.5bp.
CTA positioning is 87% of max short and futures are now through all short-term buy triggers. The desk sees elevated short covering from here as momentum signals flip to buying.

Friday unwound part of Thursday's rally, with rates cheaper across the curve. Brent closed just shy of $117/bbl on intensifying Houthi attacks on Saudi infrastructure. Rates remain torn between equity risk-off/AI concerns and higher oil. Going into FOMC week, 2.7bp of hikes are priced for the meeting and 21.4bp cumulatively by year-end.
Thursday vol was very bid and the surface flattened aggressively. 1m10y vols rose 0.5bp/day, the 8th largest move in the last 252 trading days.

Mitchell Cornell (Volex Trading): rates vol ratcheted higher into a roughly 30bp rally in TY since the cheaps on CPI day, because the rally was risk-off and flight-to-quality rather than a typical rally. Long payers / short receivers positions were hurt. Client demand for receivers stays strong and thinner liquidity amplified the vol and duration moves.

GS estimates core PCE inflation at 3.1% y/y in September versus 2.2% for the Dallas Fed trimmed mean. Tariffs, the energy shock and AI-related price pressure and mismeasurement explain about 75% of the gap. GS sees most of their sequential impact as behind us and holds that trimming still makes sense and inflation is not broadening out.

Fed speakers point to a consensus for hiking every other meeting, implying a skip in October and a hike in December. Almost all participants say further tightening is likely needed. Williams sees perhaps one more hike and Logan sees 50bp or more. Several participants' comments imply more than one additional hike.

Fed officials are split on inflation breadth. Hammack calls pressures broad-based and not just supply-side, and Goolsbee says the Fed may need to respond to persistent supply shocks. Williams and Jefferson see underlying inflation easing, though their comments predate the CPI report. Almost all participants see the labor market as in balance.

October S&P Global services PMI fell 0.9pt to 57.9, in line with consensus. New business rose 0.4pt to 58.9, employment fell 1.4pt to 53.8 and input prices fell 2.6pt to 63.4 after last month's highest reading since Nov 2022.

October S&P Global manufacturing PMI rose 0.1pt to 56.0, slightly above expectations and the highest since May 2022 if confirmed. Input prices rose 8.4pt to 74.0 and output prices rose 7.1pt to 66.1. GS says part of the survey strength reflects nominal bias.

GS (Briggs) estimates a 15% AI productivity gain could temporarily displace about 9% of workers. Each 1% productivity gain from technology historically adds a temporary 0.3-0.4pp to unemployment. Job losses, not slower hiring, drive the effect, so AI-related layoffs should be a good real-time guide. Disruption is limited in healthy economies but accelerates in cyclical slowdowns.

GS nowcasts central bank gold purchases of 79 tonnes in August versus a pre-2022 average of 17 tonnes, with 85 tonnes per month on a 3-month seasonally adjusted basis. China accounts for a large share. GS sees this as structural support for gold. Foreign central bank gold at the NY Fed fell 40 tonnes in August while custodial holdings at the Bank of England rose 46 tonnes.

FOMC week (Warsh press conference Wednesday) brings durable goods, consumer confidence and Case-Shiller Tuesday, and advance Q3 GDP with September PCE and jobless claims Thursday. Friday brings Q3 ECI and Chicago PMI. Treasury supply: 2s Monday, 5s Tuesday, 7s Thursday.

risk_factors: Oil escalation from Houthi attacks on Saudi infrastructure and unresolved Middle East tensions.
Further AI-driven equity weakness (GS AI basket -23% since June, NDX -3% Thursday) spreading to aggregate demand-relevant companies.
Rate/equity and rate/oil correlation regime switches that complicate vol and duration risk management.
Thin liquidity amplifying vol and duration moves.
French and European sovereign stress (French 10y above 5%, OAT-Bund widening).
Persistent price pressures in PMIs (manufacturing input prices at 74.0) and a firmer September CPI.
AI-related labor displacement that could amplify the business cycle in a slowdown.
vol_and_positioning: CTA positioning is 87% of max short and futures are through all short-term buy triggers. The desk expects elevated short covering as momentum signals flip to buying.
Thursday's rates vol was very bid and the surface aggressively flattened. 1m10y vols rose 0.5bp/day, the 8th largest move in the last 252 trading days.

Vol ratcheted higher into a roughly 30bp TY rally since the cheaps on CPI day. Long payers / short receivers were hurt, client receiver demand is strong, and a decent part of the vol move unwound with Friday's selloff.
Friday flows: better interest to receive Dec FOMC outright, light swap duration flows, and Hedge Funds better receivers against belly paying.
Thursday flows: Real Money two-way in swaps (better steepeners), and Hedge Funds better sellers of spreads across the curve.
Tuesday flows: Real Money receiving into the rally, steepeners fading the flattening, and light Hedge Fund buying of belly spreads.
geopolitical: Middle East tensions: oil pushed higher with no resolution, and a US-Iran deal headline briefly richened Treasuries before doubts grew.
Reuters reported the US was preparing departures of some personnel and family members from Gulf embassies, later clarified as applying only to some personnel in Saudi Arabia.
Intensifying Houthi attacks on Saudi infrastructure pushed Brent to just shy of $117/bbl on Friday.
French 10y yields topped 5% for the first time since 2002, and the 10y OAT-Bund spread widened ~15bp on Thursday.

tension_points.bull_case: GS holds that trimming still makes sense: tariffs, energy shock and AI pricing explain about 75% of the gap between 3.1% core PCE and 2.2% trimmed mean, most of their sequential impact is behind us, and inflation is not broadening out.
tension_points.bear_case: Hammack and Goolsbee argue pressures are broad-based and persistent. Trimming is weaker when outlier sources are unclear, since outliers might signal a shift in trend. Manufacturing PMI input prices at 74.0 show ongoing price pressure.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A rising share of upper-tail categories trimmed in consecutive months, which would show persistent outliers rather than normal monthly noise.

tension_points.bull_case: Receiver demand is strong and the risk-off flight-to-quality rally with CTA short covering supports duration.
tension_points.bear_case: Higher oil (Brent near $117) and firm inflation keep rates torn, and Friday's selloff unwound part of the rally.

theme_stances.key_argument: A risk-off, flight-to-quality rally came with higher vol, making risk management harder for vol traders.
theme_stances.evidence: The main story is a risk-off, flight-to-quality rally that came with higher vol.

theme_stances.key_argument: Tariffs, the energy shock and AI factors explain about 75% of the core-trimmed gap, and most of their impact is behind us.
theme_stances.evidence: inflation is not broadening out and that the trimmed mean remains a good guide

theme_stances.key_argument: EM central banks remain underweight gold and reserve diversification motives persist.
theme_stances.evidence: central bank demand as a structural support for gold
